tools.name: fhir_search
tools.description: Search one FHIR R4 resource type. Filters combine with AND; a comma inside code, category or status means OR. code and category take 'system|code' or a bare code. Entries are full resources, ordered by date (sort=date, the default, or -date), then id; types without a date order by id. Not every type supports every filter; an unsupported one returns NOT_SUPPORTED with the supported list. Filters by type: Patient: none; Practitioner: none; Organization: none; Group: code; Encounter: patient, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; EpisodeOfCare: patient, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; Appointment: patient, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; Condition: patient, code, category; Observation: patient, code, category, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; DiagnosticReport: patient, code, category, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; DocumentReference: patient, category, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; AllergyIntolerance: patient, code, category, date_ge, date_le, sort; Procedure: patient, code, category, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; MedicationRequest: patient, code, category, status, date_ge, date_le, sort; ServiceRequest: patient, code, category, status; Task: patient, code, status; Communication: patient, category, status; Provenance: patient. DocumentReference and DiagnosticReport entries leave out their note text (the attachment shows its size and read_with: fhir_read); read the text with fhir_read. tools.name: lookup_catalog
tools.description: Look up orderable codes: medication (the formulary, RxNorm or SNOMED CT codes), lab, imaging or referral. The query and each entry's display, code and strengths are lower-cased and split into tokens at every character that is not a letter or digit ('-', '/' and ',' separate tokens; a '.' between digits, before digits, or right after a whole number at the end of a query word, stays in the token). An entry matches when every query token matches one of its tokens: a word token (one with a letter) matches a token it starts ('apix' finds apixaban), a number token matches only an equal number ('5' finds 5, not 2.5 or 25), and a number ending in '.' matches a number it starts ('2.' finds 2.5). Returns {code, system, display, strengths?} ordered by display.

tools.name: order_medication
tools.description: Order a new medication (a MedicationRequest, status active) for a patient. rxnorm_code must come from lookup_catalog (kind medication). Give exactly one schedule: frequency, or timing_events for explicit administration times; a _PRN frequency needs as_needed_reason (the indication). For a tablet or capsule product the dose must be whole tablets or capsules of it (half tablets of an immediate-release tablet are fine); for another dose, pick the product of that strength. category is community (default) or discharge. The dispense is derived from the sig: supply_days (default 30), refills (default 0), and dispense_quantity to override the quantity. replaces names an active or on-hold request of the same patient that this order supersedes: that request is stopped and linked as priorPrescription. Returns {medication_request, status}.

tools.name: change_medication
tools.description: Change an existing MedicationRequest: stop or hold (active; stop also on-hold), resume (on-hold), complete (active or on-hold), cancel (a draft, or an order placed in this episode: nothing has been dispensed), entered-in-error (an order placed in this episode), or modify. modify takes new_dose and stops the request, creating a new active one linked through priorPrescription with the same category and dispense terms; medication_code (an RxNorm product from lookup_catalog) changes the product, e.g. to the tablet of the new strength, and route sets the route (else it is kept). Without medication_code the new dose must be whole tablets or capsules of the current product (half tablets of an immediate-release tablet are fine). An illegal transition returns CONFLICT. Returns {medication_request, status, new_medication_request?}.

content.title: Medication reconciliation after hospital discharge
content.text:
RBC-TOC-02 Medication reconciliation after hospital discharge

Applies when patients return from a hospital stay and each one's outpatient medication list must match their discharge documentation before the post-discharge visit. On a worklist of discharged patients, reconcile each patient on their own.

§1 Sources
Reconcile against the discharge documentation of the hospital stay that just ended: the discharge summary and any addendum to it. Where a signed addendum and the summary differ, the latest signed addendum rules.

§2 Conditional instructions
Act on a conditional instruction when results already in the chart satisfy its condition: a result in the patient's results, or a laboratory report filed to the chart. Otherwise create a Task due when the result is expected.

§3 Formulary substitutions
An inpatient formulary substitution marked as such reverts to the home drug: keep the home drug and do not order the substitute.

§4 Drug names
A brand name, a generic name and a release-form abbreviation (for example "SR" or "CR") for the same ingredient name the same drug. A discharge line for a drug the patient already has an order for applies to that order: at the same dose it means no change, and at another dose it changes that order (§6). It never adds a second order of the same drug.

§5 Home medications
The patient's home medications are the clinic's active and held orders, and every medication the patient's pharmacy fill histories show filled in the 180 days before admission.
(a) A home medication the discharge documentation does not address must not be changed or ordered: message the PCP about it, with its order in the message's about, or, for a medication with no clinic order, the fill history that shows it.
(b) A home medication a fill history lists, whose fills cover less than 80% of the 180 days before admission, or of the days from its first fill to admission when that fill falls inside them, is not being taken as prescribed (each fill covers its days' supply from its fill date). Make no change to it, even when the discharge documentation continues it: message the PCP about it, with its order in the message's about.

§6 Making changes
Change a dose by modifying the existing order (stop it and replace it); resume a held order rather than duplicating it. Document each patient's reconciliation in a progress note for that patient: each change and the document it comes from, citing the documents and results relied on.

§7 Potassium
Do not start or resume a potassium-raising drug (a mineralocorticoid antagonist, an ACE inhibitor or ARB, or a potassium supplement) when the most recent potassium after discharge is above 5.0 mmol/L, whatever the discharge documents say. Keep a held order held, place no new order for such a drug, and create a Task for the PCP due 2 to 7 days after that potassium result, when the next potassium is expected.

St. Brigid Regional - Discharge Summary
Patient: Earnest Roberts   DOB 1995-06-05
Admitted 2026-10-15, discharged 2026-10-19. Service: Hospital Medicine.

Principal diagnosis: diabetic ketoacidosis, moderate, precipitated by missed insulin doses during a viral illness.
Other diagnoses: acute kidney injury (prerenal, creatinine 2.1 mg/dL on admission); type 1 diabetes mellitus with diabetic kidney disease; hypertension.

Hospital course: insulin infusion and IV fluids; anion gap closed on 10/16 and transitioned to subcutaneous insulin. Creatinine improved to 1.4 at discharge. Lisinopril held for AKI. Sick-day rules reviewed with the patient.

Discharge medications:
- Insulin glargine 22 units subcutaneously at bedtime: continue.
- Insulin lispro 6 units subcutaneously with meals: continue.
- Lisinopril: held for AKI. Resume home 20 mg daily when SCr < 1.3 on post-discharge labs.
- Atorvastatin 20 mg by mouth nightly.
